annotation.title_clean: Proposal for a Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence (AI Liability Directive)
annotation.title_en: Proposal for a Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence (AI Liability Directive)
annotation.summary_en: European Commission's proposed AI Liability Directive harmonising aspects of non-contractual fault-based civil liability for AI. It introduces court-ordered disclosure of evidence on high-risk AI systems and a rebuttable presumption of causality, with a staged review of strict liability and mandatory insurance.
key_provisions_or_claims: Courts may order disclosure and preservation of evidence on suspected high-risk AI systems (Art. 3).
Failure to comply with a disclosure order triggers a rebuttable presumption of breach of duty of care.
Rebuttable presumption of causal link between fault and AI output under defined conditions (Art. 4).
Minimum harmonisation; does not alter definitions of fault, damage or burden of proof generally.
Commission review five years after transposition on strict liability and mandatory insurance (Art. 5).
